finding.description: Describes a defect in the same-role review, not a candidate defect already captured by a supported review finding.

reviewFindingAdjudication.description: Judges one finding made by the same-role review rather than judging the candidate defect again.

findingIds.description: Links only adjudicator findings that explain why this review finding is rejected; this array is empty when judgment is supported.

surfaceAdjudication.description: Echoes the bound same-role review assessment in reviewAssessmentJudgment and judges the soundness of that assessment in judgment. A sound blocking review assessment is blocking plus supported, not an adjudication failure.

findingIds.description: Links only adjudicator findings that explain a rejected same-role review assessment. It is empty for supported; rejected requires a linked blocking finding on this surface.

judgment.description: supported approves the same-role review assessment even when reviewAssessmentJudgment is blocking; rejected means the assessment is unsound or incomplete.

reviewAssessmentJudgment.description: Exact echo of the bound same-role review assessment's judgment; the deterministic verifier rejects any mismatch.

adjudicationSchema.description: This record judges the soundness and completeness of the same-role review, not the candidate.

findings.description: Adjudicator findings describe defects in the same-role review's requirement, assessment, reasoning, finding, coverage, or severity; they do not repeat candidate defects already captured by supported review findings.

reviewFindingAdjudications.description: Each entry judges one same-role review finding. A supported review finding has no adjudicator-finding links; a rejected review finding requires a linked blocking adjudicator finding that explains the review defect.

surfaceAdjudications.description: Each entry exactly echoes the same-role review assessment's pass, advisory, or blocking judgment, then separately judges that assessment as supported or rejected; it does not judge the candidate surface directly.

verdict.description: pass means the same-role review is sound and complete, even when that review correctly fails the candidate; fail means the same-role review is unsound or incomplete. This verdict never judges the candidate directly.

adjudicationSchema.title: Independent canonical-English semantic adjudication record

adjudicationSemantics.failMeaning: The same-role review is unsound or incomplete.
adjudicationSemantics.findingLinkMeaning: A supported surface assessment or review finding has no adjudicator-finding links; a rejected one links at least one blocking adjudicator finding on an overlapping surface that explains a defect in the review.
adjudicationSemantics.passMeaning: The same-role review is sound and complete, even when that review correctly fails the candidate.
adjudicationSemantics.subject: same-role-review
adjudicationSemantics.surfaceAdjudicationMeaning: Each surface adjudication exactly echoes the bound review assessment judgment in reviewAssessmentJudgment, then uses judgment supported or rejected to judge that assessment.

reviewBundle.inventoryLimitation: This evidence covers only the explicitly declared inventory. Completeness and classification of learner-facing surfaces remain reviewer-judged; the tool does not discover or certify omitted surfaces.
reviewBundle.rubric:
# Isolated-surface criteria

Assess every supplied unit as its complete frozen isolation boundary and in its
stated actual role. Repeat the frozen role requirement exactly; do not invent,
narrow or replace it, split a legitimately grouped unit, or assume unavailable
surrounding material.

Check coherent English, grammar, technical register, explicit referents, actors,
operations, conditions, comparisons, quantities, units, mappings, scope, actions
and destinations required by that role. Standalone copy must carry its necessary
referents. Contextual headings and genuinely associated groups need not repeat
the whole lesson or every limitation beyond their frozen role requirement.

Judge accessibility meaning from the supplied words and language-neutral
literals, not unseen styling, colors, position, interface chrome or presumed
author intent. An accessible description must state the relationships needed
for its stated purpose; numerical values alone may not explain them.

Give a distinct substantive rationale for every unit. Apply the schema's
severity and verdict rules consistently. Do not infer a suspected correction or
expected outcome from a unit's identifier. A clean pass is valid; do not invent
findings or an expected verdict. Return judgments only, not revised copy.
